I've mapped it. Aesel already follows media the agent touches, but only in the pro profile. I'm widening that to every session and adding focus rules now.
Now the helpers in media.mjs.
The focus rules are in. Next, I'm making a new artifact revision take the card back, and checking the restore path.
The full suite ran, and the new focus tests pass. Two tests failed, both in areas I didn't touch: render scrolling and a network timeout. I'm confirming where they live.

Aesel now follows focus. The preview turns to whatever was made last, in every session, not just in pro. It isn't committed yet. Restart Aesel to pick it up.

The tests for the two new rules pass. I haven't seen it switch in a live Aesel window yet, because Aesel wasn't running for this session.

It switches like this:

- **When the agent makes a file:** a jpg, png, webp, wav, mp3, pdf or video turns the preview to it.
  - A file counts only if the tool call actually wrote it during that call. Reading a reference image or converting from an old file doesn't steal focus.
  - Pro used to switch on any file a tool mentioned. Now it also switches only on files that were written.
- **When the agent edits the piece:** the preview goes back to the live piece.
- **When an artifact gets a new revision:** the preview goes back to the artifact. The 30-second artifact refresh no longer pulls focus off a file on its own.
- **When you name a file:** a message like "swap to the webp" switches to the newest file of that kind the preview has shown. A file name or full path works too. Only this path also clears a borrowed `/preview notepat`.
- **A pin still holds:** `/preview <file>`, or pinning from the media list, keeps the preview on that file until you unpin.

The new rules are `madeMedia` and `namedMedia` in `aesel/src/media.mjs`, with tests in `test/media.test.mjs`. The wiring is in `aesel/src/tui.mjs`, at `noteMedia`, `focusMedia`, `notePiece`, `announceArtifact` and the submit path.

Two other tests in the full suite fail: a scroll-layout test in `tui-performance.test.mjs` and a timeout test in `draft-broadcast.test.mjs`. Neither touches media or focus. `tui-performance.test.mjs` and `render.mjs` already had uncommitted changes from another session. I didn't touch the timeout test's file, but I didn't check whether it was already failing.

GIFs still won't show, because Slab's preview only accepts png, jpeg and webp images.

I left everything uncommitted because `tui.mjs` also holds that other session's work.
